          Manchester United 3-2 Roma Stats: Late Cunha Brace Completes Stunning Turnaround
        
      
                          
                      Nov 3, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the pressure mounting on Michael Carrick at half-time, Manchester United ended their long winless streak with a superb comeback to defeat Roma 3-2 in the UEFA Champions League.
Matheus Cunha‘s late brace completed a remarkable second-half turnaround, earning Manchester United a much-needed 3-2 win over Roma in the Champions League.
It looked like United's woes were set to continue as they found themselves 2-0 down after 17 minutes at Old Trafford, with Matías Soulé and Donyell Malen getting the goals.

However, Bruno Fernandes halved the deficit from the penalty spot before Cunha scored twice in the space of just under three minutes to help lift some of the pressure on Michael Carrick's shoulders, before receiving a stoppage-time red card.
It took Roma 11 minutes to carve United open when Rodrigo Mora switched play to the unmarked Soulé, who had time to take a touch before slotting into the bottom-right corner.
Things then went from bad to worse just six minutes later when Harry Maguire gifted Soulé possession in the box. Ayden Heaven threw himself into the block but made it with his outstretched arm.
Malen then made no mistake from 12 yards, firing past Senne Lammens, who dived the wrong way.
Roma finished the first half strongly, with Malen seeing a low drive palmed away by Lammens before Soulé ‘s curler skimmed the outside of the left post on the stroke of half-time.

However, United came out brighter in the second half – despite losing Carlos Baleba to a hamstring injury shortly after the break – and were given a route back in when Gianluca Mancini was punished for a clumsy tangle with Cunha.
Fernandes' first spot-kick was saved by debutant Devis Vásquez, but it was retaken due to Roma encroachment, and the United captain emphatically blasted in his second attempt in the 58th minute.
He then threaded it in behind for Bryan Mbeumo, but his shot hit the left post, bounced across the goal line and back out off the opposite stick.
Maguire saw a header blocked by Wesley and caused more issues from the resulting corner, nodding it across for Diogo Dalot, who was denied on the line by Bryan Cristante.
United's pressure eventually told again in the 83rd minute, with Leonardo Balerdi missing his attempted clearance, and Cunha was hovering behind to turn in from close range.
He got his second in the 86th minute, putting his laces through the tight-angled effort on the right of the box to get the better of Vasquez at his near post.

It prompted wild celebrations, with Cunha whipping off his shirt and leaping into the crowd, and it cost him in the 91st minute as he received his second booking for a late tackle on Balerdi, though United held out to end their nine-game winless streak.

The first 20 minutes of the match summed up United's recent struggles as they were carved wide open, with Dalot punished for being caught upfield when Soule opened the scoring, and things did not get any easier when Malen converted the penalty.

United have conceded first in four successive games for the first time since May 2025, while this is the earliest a team have scored twice as the visiting side at Old Trafford in major European competition.

It is no surprise that Malen was on the scoresheet, though. Since his Roma debut in January, he has scored 27 goals in all competitions – only Harry Kane (39) has scored more times for a club in Europe's big five leagues in that period.

But Carrick was part of a United squad years ago that were no stranger to overturning the odds to get three points by coming from behind, and they ran back the years by coming from two goals down at half-time to win for the first time since October 2021 against Gian Piero Gasperini's Atalanta (also 3-2).
Fernandes had failed to score with his previous 18 shots across all competitions before stepping up to take his 50th United penalty. He has now scored 44 of them.
